BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the basis of division first. 2) the tree from the top down. 3) each kind with its identifying feature and an example. 4) the borderline cases and exceptions. 5) the tree as recap.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

Video v1: Tissue क्या है? Cell से पूरे शरीर तक
Goal: तुम tissue की definition, division of labour, biological organisation और animal tissues का पूरा visual overview समझोगे।
Opening hook: शरीर के सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते?
Story or analogy: काम बाँटकर चलती team से division of labour समझाएँगे; फिर book के cell–tissue–organ–organ system–organism क्रम पर लौटेंगे।
Planned minutes: 9
Narration time (S2-01): 7.7-10.3 minutes, about 1001-1339 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and basic plant-cell parts; Chromosome sets, DNA copying and nuclear versus cell division; Body covering, cavity, lumen and gland duct; Diffusion, absorption and secretion; Strength, flexibility, elasticity and rigidity; Contraction, relaxation, fatigue and voluntary control; Root and shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth; Photosynthesis, food storage and root water–mineral uptake

Items (item id | page | kind | type | content), each with its teacher questions (question id | ask | question → answer | basis):
p001-i2 | 1 | definition | definition | TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function.
  p001-i2#q1 | what | What does the page mean by tissue? → A tissue is a grouping of cells that work together to perform the same function. | book
  p001-i2#q2 | evidence | What defining feature does the page give for recognising a tissue? → It links the combination of cells to their shared function; merely naming a collection of cells leaves out this functional connection. | book
  p001-i2#q3 | how | How does a group of cells function as a tissue? → Cells coordinate their activities and contribute to a common task. For example, muscle cells collectively produce contraction. | outside
p001-i3 | 1 | list_point | classification | • When plant cells combine, they form plant tissues.
  p001-i3#q1 | which | Which cells form plant tissues? → Plant tissues are formed by the combination of plant cells. | book
  p001-i3#q2 | difference | How does this category differ from animal tissue on the page? → The distinction here is the kind of organism supplying the cells: plant cells form plant tissues, while animal cells form animal tissues. | book
  p001-i3#q3 | how | How should 'combine' be understood in a growing plant? → Cells produced during growth remain organised into groups and may differentiate for common functions; the wording need not imply that separate cells fuse into one cell. | outside
p001-i4 | 1 | list_point | classification | • When animal cells combine, they form animal tissues.
  p001-i4#q1 | which | Which cells form animal tissues? → Animal tissues are formed from animal cells acting together. | book
  p001-i4#q2 | difference | What separates animal tissues from plant tissues in these introductory bullets? → Animal tissues consist of animal cells; plant tissues consist of plant cells. | book
  p001-i4#q3 | how | How can animal cells contribute to a common tissue function? → They acquire specialised properties and coordinate their activity, as nerve cells do in receiving and transmitting signals. | outside
p001-i5 | 1 | list_point | cause_effect | • Causes division of labour.
  p001-i5#q1 | why | Why does the page connect tissues with division of labour? → It presents tissue formation as enabling cells to share the work of the organism. | book
  p001-i5#q2 | how | How does division of labour operate between tissues? → Different tissues specialise in different tasks, such as protection, transport or movement, so the organism's work is distributed among specialised groups. | outside
  p001-i5#q3 | why | Why can specialisation improve performance? → A cell's shape, internal machinery and activity can be suited to a particular task, improving its contribution to that task while other cells perform complementary roles. | outside
p001-i6 | 1 | list_point | cause_effect | • Decreases workload on individual cells, hence leads to organisation.
  p001-i6#q1 | why | Why does the page say tissues decrease the workload on individual cells? → It connects grouping cells into tissues with distributing work, rather than placing the organism's work on individual cells. | book
  p001-i6#q2 | how | How does distributing work lead to organisation? → Specialised cells form tissues; different tissues cooperate in organs; organs cooperate in organ systems. This produces coordinated levels of organisation. | outside
  p001-i6#q3 | exception | Does reduced workload mean a specialised cell stops carrying out its own life processes? → No. It still maintains itself, including using energy and synthesising required molecules. The shared workload concerns the wider functions of the organism. | outside
p001-i7 | 1 | diagram | structure | Cell → Tissues → Organ → Organ system → Organisms. Each rightward arrow connects a smaller biological level to the larger level into which it is organised.
  p001-i7#q1 | what | What hierarchy does the sequence show? → It orders biological organisation from cell to tissue, organ, organ system and organism. | book
  p001-i7#q2 | where | Where are tissues and organs placed in the hierarchy? → Tissues lie between cells and organs; organs lie between tissues and organ systems. | book
  p001-i7#q3 | how | How should the arrows be interpreted? → They express organisational membership: cells make up tissues, tissues make up organs, and organs work in systems within an organism. They do not mean that one isolated cell simply turns into an entire organism through these named stages. | outside
p001-i8 | 1 | diagram_label | structure | Cell: first level; arrow leads to Tissues.
  p001-i8#q1 | what | What does Cell name here? → The starting level in the organisation sequence. | book
  p001-i8#q2 | where | Where is Cell positioned? → Before Tissues, at the left end. | book
  p001-i8#q3 | how | How do cells contribute to the next level? → Groups of cells coordinate a shared function to form a tissue. | book
p001-i9 | 1 | diagram_label | structure | Tissues: between Cell and Organ.
  p001-i9#q1 | what | What does Tissues identify? → The level formed by cells and preceding organs. | book
  p001-i9#q2 | where | Where are tissues in the sequence? → After Cell and before Organ. | book
  p001-i9#q3 | how | How can tissues contribute to an organ? → Different tissues cooperate in an organ; for example, muscle, connective and nervous tissues contribute to the heart. | outside
p001-i10 | 1 | diagram_label | structure | Organ: between Tissues and Organ system.
  p001-i10#q1 | what | What does Organ represent? → The organisational level between tissues and organ systems. | book
  p001-i10#q2 | where | Where is Organ placed? → After Tissues and before Organ system. | book
  p001-i10#q3 | how | How is an organ organised internally? → Several tissues are arranged to perform related functions, as in a leaf or a heart. | outside
p001-i11 | 1 | diagram_label | structure | Organ system: between Organ and Organisms.
  p001-i11#q1 | what | What does Organ system identify? → The level above an organ and below the complete organism. | book
  p001-i11#q2 | where | Where is Organ system in the sequence? → Between Organ and Organisms. | book
  p001-i11#q3 | how | How do organs function together as a system? → They perform complementary tasks within a larger function; digestive organs, for example, cooperate in processing food and absorbing nutrients. | outside
p001-i12 | 1 | diagram_label | structure | Organisms: final level, following Organ system.
  p001-i12#q1 | what | What does Organisms name at the end? → The complete living beings at the highest level shown. | book
  p001-i12#q2 | where | Where is this label located? → At the right end, after Organ system. | book
  p001-i12#q3 | how | How do systems support an organism? → Their activities are coordinated so that needs such as nutrition, transport and waste removal are met together. | outside
p002-i1 | 2 | diagram | figure | Animal Tissues classification tree. Animal Tissues branches into Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue and Nervous / Neural Tissue. Muscular Tissue branches into Striated muscle, Non-striated muscle and Cardiac muscle. Connective Tissue branches into Connective tissue proper, Supportive connective tissue and Fluid connective tissue. Connective tissue proper branches into Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue. Supportive connective tissue branches into Cartilage and Bone. Fluid connective tissue branches into Blood and Lymph. Epithelial Tissue connects by a long descending line to Simple squamous epithelium, Stratified squamous epithelium, Columnar epithelium, Ciliated columnar epithelium, Cuboidal epithelium and Glandular epithelium. Nervous / Neural Tissue has no further branch on this chart.
  p002-i1#q1 | what | What does this tree show? → It organises animal tissues into four main groups and then shows the named subdivisions of epithelial, muscular and connective tissues. | book
  p002-i1#q2 | which | Which parent-child relationships are especially important to read correctly? → Blood and lymph belong to fluid connective tissue; cartilage and bone belong to supportive connective tissue; areolar, adipose and fibrous tissues belong to connective tissue proper. The six epithelial labels belong to Epithelial Tissue despite the long connecting line. | book
  p002-i1#q3 | how | How should a learner follow a classification branch? → Start at Animal Tissues, follow a connecting line to a main group, and continue along its branches to a subtype. The arrows express membership in a group, not a sequence in which one tissue changes into another. | book
p002-i2 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Animal Tissues: root label connected to four main tissue groups.
  p002-i2#q1 | what | What is the root topic of this diagram? → Animal Tissues is the overall group being divided into tissue types. | book
  p002-i2#q2 | which | Which four groups arise directly from it? → Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue and Nervous / Neural Tissue. | book
  p002-i2#q3 | why | Why does an animal body contain different tissue groups? → Different groups of cells specialise in covering surfaces, producing movement, supporting or connecting parts, and transmitting information. | outside
p002-i3 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Epithelial Tissue: main branch leading to six epithelial labels along the bottom of the tree.
  p002-i3#q1 | what | What does the Epithelial Tissue branch represent? → It is one of the four main animal tissue groups in the chart. | book
  p002-i3#q2 | which | Which types are connected to it? → Simple squamous, stratified squamous, columnar, ciliated columnar, cuboidal and glandular epithelium. | book
  p002-i3#q3 | how | How does epithelial organisation suit a covering or lining role? → Closely packed cells form continuous sheets, making a surface that can protect, absorb or secrete according to its specialisation. | outside
p002-i4 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Muscular Tissue: main branch connected to Striated muscle, Non-striated muscle and Cardiac muscle.
  p002-i4#q1 | what | What group does this label identify? → It identifies muscular tissue as a main animal tissue group. | book
  p002-i4#q2 | which | Which muscle types does the chart show? → Striated muscle, Non-striated muscle and Cardiac muscle. | book
  p002-i4#q3 | how | How does muscular tissue produce movement? → Its cells contain contractile proteins that generate force, allowing movement of body parts or material within organs. | outside
p002-i5 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Connective Tissue: main branch connected to Connective tissue proper, Supportive connective tissue and Fluid connective tissue.
  p002-i5#q1 | what | What does this branch identify? → It identifies connective tissue as a main animal tissue group with three subdivisions on this page. | book
  p002-i5#q2 | which | Which subdivisions are shown? → Connective tissue proper, supportive connective tissue and fluid connective tissue. | book
  p002-i5#q3 | how | How can connective tissues include such different examples as bone and blood? → Connective tissues have cells associated with an extracellular matrix. The matrix differs between tissues, being mineralised in bone and fluid in blood. | outside
p002-i6 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Nervous / Neural Tissue: fourth main branch, with no subtypes drawn.
  p002-i6#q1 | what | What does 'Nervous / Neural Tissue' name? → The chart uses nervous and neural as alternative names for this main tissue group. | book
  p002-i6#q2 | which | Which subdivisions are shown beneath this label? → None are shown on this chart. | book
  p002-i6#q3 | how | How does nervous tissue help coordinate the body? → Neurons receive and transmit signals, while supporting cells help maintain the conditions needed for nervous tissue to function. | outside
p002-i7 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Striated muscle: left subtype under Muscular Tissue.
  p002-i7#q1 | what | What is the parent group of Striated muscle? → It is shown under Muscular Tissue. | book
  p002-i7#q2 | which | Which lower illustration corresponds to this category in the chart's usage? → The skeletal muscle illustration corresponds to the category called striated muscle here. | outside
  p002-i7#q3 | why | Why must the word striated be used carefully? → It refers to visible bands caused by organised contractile proteins. Skeletal muscle is striated, but cardiac muscle also has striations even though the chart gives it a separate branch. | outside
p002-i8 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Non-striated muscle: middle subtype under Muscular Tissue.
  p002-i8#q1 | what | What does the chart place under muscular tissue in the middle branch? → Non-striated muscle. | book
  p002-i8#q2 | which | Which name in the lower muscle panel corresponds to non-striated muscle? → Smooth muscle is the corresponding name. | outside
  p002-i8#q3 | why | Why is this muscle described as non-striated? → Its contractile proteins are not arranged into the regular banded units seen in skeletal and cardiac muscle, so visible cross-striations are absent. | outside
p002-i9 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Cardiac muscle: right subtype under Muscular Tissue.
  p002-i9#q1 | what | What position does cardiac muscle occupy in the tree? → It is one of the three branches of Muscular Tissue. | book
  p002-i9#q2 | which | Which organ contains cardiac muscle? → The heart contains cardiac muscle in its muscular wall. | outside
  p002-i9#q3 | how | How does cardiac muscle serve the heart? → Its coordinated, involuntary contractions generate the force that pumps blood. | outside
p002-i10 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Connective tissue proper: branch leading to Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue.
  p002-i10#q1 | what | What is connective tissue proper in this chart? → It is one of the three subdivisions of Connective Tissue. | book
  p002-i10#q2 | which | Which examples belong to it? → Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue. | book
  p002-i10#q3 | how | How can its examples have different roles? → Their proportions of cells, fibres and ground substance differ, allowing loose packing, fat storage or strong attachment. | outside
p002-i11 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Supportive connective tissue: branch leading to Cartilage and Bone.
  p002-i11#q1 | what | What does this label identify? → A subdivision of connective tissue labelled Supportive connective tissue. | book
  p002-i11#q2 | which | Which two tissues are grouped here? → Cartilage and Bone. | book
  p002-i11#q3 | how | How do these tissues provide support differently? → Cartilage has a firm but flexible matrix; bone has a mineralised matrix that gives greater rigidity. | outside
p002-i12 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Fluid connective tissue: branch leading to Blood and Lymph.
  p002-i12#q1 | what | What is the fluid subdivision of connective tissue called? → Fluid connective tissue. | book
  p002-i12#q2 | which | Which tissues are included? → Blood and Lymph. | book
  p002-i12#q3 | why | Why can these tissues perform transport roles? → Their fluid medium allows cells and dissolved substances to move between body regions. | outside
p002-i13 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Areolar tissue: leaf under Connective tissue proper.
  p002-i13#q1 | what | What is the chart's classification of areolar tissue? → It belongs to connective tissue proper. | book
  p002-i13#q2 | which | Which tissues share its immediate parent? → Adipose tissue and Fibrous tissue. | book
  p002-i13#q3 | how | How does areolar tissue help hold body structures together? → Its loosely arranged fibres and matrix form packing tissue that supports and binds neighbouring structures while permitting some movement. | outside
p002-i14 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Adipose tissue: leaf under Connective tissue proper.
  p002-i14#q1 | what | What group contains adipose tissue? → Connective tissue proper. | book
  p002-i14#q2 | which | Which lower illustration helps recognise adipose tissue? → The connective tissue panel includes Fat cells and a label for Fat and other Soft padding tissue. | book
  p002-i14#q3 | how | How do adipose cells contribute to the body? → They store lipid, providing an energy reserve; adipose deposits also cushion structures and help reduce heat loss. | outside
p002-i15 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Fibrous tissue: leaf under Connective tissue proper.
  p002-i15#q1 | what | What group contains fibrous tissue? → Connective tissue proper. | book
  p002-i15#q2 | which | Which lower example illustrates a strong fibrous connective structure? → The tendon illustration is an example of dense fibrous connective tissue. | outside
  p002-i15#q3 | why | Why are fibres important in this tissue? → Abundant collagen fibres resist pulling forces and make strong attachments possible. | outside
p002-i16 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Cartilage: leaf under Supportive connective tissue.
  p002-i16#q1 | what | What is cartilage classified as here? → Supportive connective tissue. | book
  p002-i16#q2 | which | Which tissue shares its immediate branch? → Bone. | book
  p002-i16#q3 | how | How does cartilage combine support with flexibility? → Its firm matrix resists deformation while remaining more flexible than mineralised bone, which suits structures such as the external ear and joint surfaces. | outside
p002-i17 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Bone: leaf under Supportive connective tissue.
  p002-i17#q1 | what | What is the classification of bone in this tree? → Bone is supportive connective tissue. | book
  p002-i17#q2 | which | Which tissue is paired with bone under the same subdivision? → Cartilage. | book
  p002-i17#q3 | why | Why is bone suited to rigid support? → Mineral salts strengthen its collagen-containing matrix, enabling it to bear loads and protect organs. | outside
p002-i18 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Blood: leaf under Fluid connective tissue.
  p002-i18#q1 | what | What type of connective tissue is blood? → Fluid connective tissue. | book
  p002-i18#q2 | which | Which other tissue is grouped with blood? → Lymph. | book
  p002-i18#q3 | how | How does blood's composition support transport? → Plasma carries dissolved substances, while blood cells perform roles such as oxygen transport and defence. | outside
p002-i19 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Lymph: leaf under Fluid connective tissue.
  p002-i19#q1 | what | What is lymph classified as here? → Fluid connective tissue. | book
  p002-i19#q2 | which | Which tissue shares its immediate parent? → Blood. | book
  p002-i19#q3 | how | How does lymph connect tissue fluid with circulation? → Excess fluid between cells enters lymphatic vessels as lymph and is eventually returned to the bloodstream; lymph also participates in immune defence. | outside
p002-i20 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Simple squamous epithelium: first leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i20#q1 | what | What epithelial subtype is named here? → Simple squamous epithelium. | book
  p002-i20#q2 | which | Which structural features do the words simple and squamous describe? → Simple means one cell layer; squamous means flattened cells. | outside
  p002-i20#q3 | why | Why is a thin epithelial sheet useful? → A short distance across the sheet facilitates diffusion and filtration, as in specialised exchange surfaces. | outside
p002-i21 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Stratified squamous epithelium: second leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i21#q1 | what | What epithelial subtype is shown beside simple squamous epithelium? → Stratified squamous epithelium. | book
  p002-i21#q2 | which | Which feature separates stratified from simple epithelium? → Stratified epithelium has several cell layers; simple epithelium has one. In stratified squamous epithelium, the surface cells are flattened. | outside
  p002-i21#q3 | why | Why are several layers useful on surfaces exposed to wear? → Layers beneath the surface maintain a protective barrier as exposed cells are damaged or shed. | outside
p002-i22 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Columnar epithelium: third leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i22#q1 | what | What epithelial subtype is named here? → Columnar epithelium. | book
  p002-i22#q2 | which | Which cell shape does columnar describe? → Cells taller than they are wide, resembling columns. | outside
  p002-i22#q3 | how | How can columnar cells support absorption and secretion? → Their height provides space for cellular machinery, and some have surface specialisations that increase absorption or aid secretion. | outside
p002-i23 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Ciliated columnar epithelium: fourth leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i23#q1 | what | What specialised columnar epithelium does the chart name? → Ciliated columnar epithelium. | book
  p002-i23#q2 | which | Which feature distinguishes it from non-ciliated columnar epithelium? → It bears cilia on its exposed surface. | outside
  p002-i23#q3 | how | How do cilia help epithelial tissue? → Coordinated beating moves material along the surface, such as mucus in ciliated respiratory passages. | outside
p002-i24 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Cuboidal epithelium: fifth leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i24#q1 | what | What epithelial subtype is named here? → Cuboidal epithelium. | book
  p002-i24#q2 | which | Which cell shape does cuboidal describe? → Cells with approximately similar height and width. | outside
  p002-i24#q3 | how | How does cuboidal epithelium function in kidney tubules? → The cells transport substances between the tubule contents and surrounding tissue, contributing to absorption and secretion. | outside
p002-i25 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Glandular epithelium: sixth leaf under Epithelial Tissue.
  p002-i25#q1 | what | What epithelial subtype completes the chart? → Glandular epithelium. | book
  p002-i25#q2 | which | Which specialisation does glandular describe? → Specialisation for secretion, rather than a particular cell shape. | outside
  p002-i25#q3 | how | How do glandular epithelial cells perform this role? → They make and release substances such as mucus, digestive enzymes or hormones, depending on the gland. | outside

p002-i28 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Muscle cells: label with leader lines grouping the illustrated muscle forms.
  p002-i28#q1 | what | What does the Muscle cells label identify? → The illustrated cellular forms in the muscular tissue panel. | book
  p002-i28#q2 | which | Which muscle examples are represented? → Cardiac, skeletal and smooth muscle. | book
  p002-i28#q3 | how | How is a muscle cell specialised? → It contains contractile proteins that use cellular energy to develop tension and, in suitable conditions, shorten. | outside
p002-i29 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Cardiac muscle: label beneath a red branching muscle drawing, associated with the heart region.
  p002-i29#q1 | what | What appearance is used for cardiac muscle? → A branching red muscle drawing. | book
  p002-i29#q2 | which | Which body region is associated with it? → The heart region in the central body illustration. | book
  p002-i29#q3 | how | How do connected cardiac cells help the heart work? → Specialised junctions mechanically connect cells and allow electrical activity to spread, helping coordinate contraction. | outside
p002-i30 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Skeletal muscle: label beneath a bundle of long red cylindrical muscle fibres.
  p002-i30#q1 | what | What form does the skeletal muscle drawing show? → A bundle of elongated cylindrical fibres with visible fibre ends. | book
  p002-i30#q2 | which | Which upper-chart category corresponds to skeletal muscle? → The category labelled Striated muscle. | outside
  p002-i30#q3 | how | How does skeletal muscle move a limb? → Contraction pulls through attachments, commonly tendons, to move bones around joints. | outside
p002-i31 | 2 | diagram_label | figure | Smooth muscle: label beneath elongated red spindle-shaped cells with tapered ends.

  p002-i31#q2 | which | Which term in the upper chart corresponds to smooth muscle? → Non-striated muscle. | outside
  p002-i31#q3 | how | How does smooth muscle help a hollow organ such as the intestine? → Coordinated involuntary contractions of the wall mix and propel its contents. | outside

frame.process: Tissue organisation distributes the organism's work.
frame.how: Shared work reduces the wider workload placed on individual cells.

beats.say: तुम्हारे शरीर के सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते? आज इसी सवाल से tissue समझेंगे, फिर cell से पूरे शरीर तक का रास्ता और animal tissues का पूरा चित्र पढ़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Question beside a body outline: सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते?

beats.say: Muscle cells को साथ काम करते सोचो। कई cells मिलकर contraction में हिस्सा लेते हैं; यहाँ सिर्फ cells का ढेर नहीं, एक साझा काम करने वाला group है।
beats.on_screen: Several muscle cells contracting together.

beats.say: Book की definition है: Cells combine to perform same function। Cells यानी काम करने वाली units; combine यानी group में साथ आना; same function यानी एक ही काम में हिस्सा देना। इसी group को tissue कहते हैं।
beats.on_screen: TISSUE: Cells combine to perform same function. Highlight each phrase.

beats.say: अगर किसी तस्वीर में कुछ अलग-अलग cells साथ रख दिए, क्या वही tissue हो गया? नहीं; सिर्फ पास दिखना काफी नहीं, उनके group का साझा function भी होना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Arbitrary cell collection versus functionally organised group.

beats.say: अब इसी definition का इस्तेमाल plant tissues और animal tissues समझने में करेंगे। दोनों में cells का group है; फर्क यह देखना है कि cells किसके हैं।
beats.on_screen: Tissue branches toward plant and animal.

beats.say: यहाँ बाँटने का आधार cells का plant या animal होना है। अभी आधार उनके आकार या काम का नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Basis: plant cells or animal cells.

beats.say: ऊपर tissue रखो और नीचे 2 रास्ते बनाओ। Plant cells मिलें तो plant tissues; animal cells मिलें तो animal tissues।
beats.on_screen: Tissue → Plant tissues / Animal tissues.

beats.say: Plant की leaf का tissue plant cells से बनता है। तुम्हारे शरीर का muscle tissue animal cells से बनता है; example बदलने पर भी पहचान का यही आधार रहेगा।
beats.on_screen: Leaf tissue and human muscle tissue beside their branches.

beats.say: Combine का मतलब यह मत लेना कि सारे cells जुड़कर 1 ही cell बन गए। यहाँ cells का organised group समझना है, जो साथ काम करता है।
beats.on_screen: Grouped cells retain individual boundaries; reject fusion interpretation.

beats.say: तो इस छोटे tree को cells से पहचानो: plant cells से plant tissues, animal cells से animal tissues। अब सवाल है, ऐसे groups बनने का फायदा क्या है?
beats.on_screen: Completed two-branch tree.

beats.say: इसका फायदा है individual cells पर काम का बोझ कम होना और organisation बनना। पूरे शरीर का हर काम हर cell को अकेले नहीं करना पड़ता।
beats.on_screen: Shared work → reduced individual workload → organisation.

beats.say: एक team सोचो: कोई सामान सँभाले, कोई उसे पहुँचाए। काम बाँटने को division of labour कहते हैं; tissue formation भी cells के बीच शरीर का काम बाँटने में मदद करती है।
beats.on_screen: Team sharing tasks, then switch to cell groups.

beats.say: अलग tissues अलग काम सँभालते हैं, जैसे covering या movement। Cells का group एक काम में हिस्सा देता है, इसलिए शरीर के सारे काम का बोझ हर individual cell पर नहीं आता।
beats.on_screen: Different tissue groups share covering and movement tasks.

beats.say: Book भी यही connection देती है: tissues से division of labour, individual cells का workload कम, और उससे organisation। ध्यान दो, ये अलग रटने वाले points नहीं, एक जुड़ी हुई बात है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the book's linked claims as a causal chain.

beats.say: लेकिन workload कम होने का मतलब cell का अपना जीवन रुकना नहीं है। उसे अपनी देखभाल और energy की जरूरत रहती है; बाँटा गया काम पूरे शरीर के काम से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Shared body work does not eliminate cellular maintenance.

beats.say: Chain वापस जोड़ो: cells के functional groups, फिर division of labour, फिर कम individual workload और organisation। अब देखो, यही organisation कितने levels पर बनी है।
beats.on_screen: Functional groups → division of labour → reduced workload → organisation.

beats.say: पूरा living being organism है। Book का क्रम Cell से शुरू होकर Tissues, Organ, Organ system और आखिर में Organisms तक जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Full hierarchy beside a complete organism.

beats.say: पूरे शरीर से अंदर देखो: Organisms से पहले Organ system है। उससे छोटा level Organ, उसके अंदर Tissues, और इस क्रम की शुरुआत में Cell है।
beats.on_screen: Nested zoom: organism → system → organ → tissue → cell.

beats.say: Cells साझा काम के लिए tissue बनाते हैं। कई tissues organ में साथ काम करते हैं; organs मिलकर system का बड़ा काम सँभालते हैं, और systems मिलकर organism को चलाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Connect each nested level to its contribution.

beats.say: इसलिए arrows का मतलब छोटे level का बड़े level में organised होना है। यह किसी अकेले cell के बारी-बारी tissue, फिर organ बन जाने की समय वाली कहानी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Arrows labelled organisation, not time or transformation.

beats.say: अब labels बाएँ से पढ़ो: Cell, Tissues, Organ, Organ system, Organisms। Tissue की जगह याद रखो: cell के बाद, organ से पहले।
beats.on_screen: Labelled left-to-right hierarchy.

beats.say: अब page 2 का chart animal tissues की categories दिखाता है। नीचे body के आसपास बड़े drawings हैं, ताकि category के साथ उसका रूप और शरीर से connection भी दिखे।
beats.on_screen: Full upper classification tree and lower body overview.

beats.say: ऊपर Animal Tissues से शुरू करो। इसकी 4 main branches हैं: Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue और Nervous / Neural Tissue; line पकड़कर नीचे subtype तक जाओ, ये बदलाव के stages नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace root to each of four main branches.

beats.say: Epithelial Tissue की लंबी line नीचे 6 labels तक जाती है। पहले Simple squamous epithelium और Stratified squamous epithelium पढ़ो; दोनों इसी main branch के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace long epithelial connector; highlight first two leaves.

beats.say: आगे Columnar epithelium और Ciliated columnar epithelium हैं। फिर Cuboidal epithelium और Glandular epithelium; इन सभी 6 का parent Epithelial Tissue ही है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight remaining four epithelial leaves and their shared connector.

beats.say: अब Muscular Tissue की branch देखो। इसके नीचे बाएँ Striated muscle, बीच में Non-striated muscle और दाएँ Cardiac muscle है।
beats.on_screen: Trace the three muscular branches left to right.

beats.say: Connective Tissue के नीचे पहले 3 groups पढ़ो: Connective tissue proper, Supportive connective tissue और Fluid connective tissue। ये बीच वाले levels हैं, इनके नीचे भी examples हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight three intermediate connective categories.

beats.say: Connective tissue proper से Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue और Fibrous tissue निकलते हैं। तीनों एक ही immediate parent के नीचे हैं; इन्हें अलग main tissue groups मत मान लेना।
beats.on_screen: Trace connective tissue proper to its three leaves.

beats.say: Supportive connective tissue में Cartilage और Bone की जोड़ी है। Fluid connective tissue में Blood और Lymph हैं; इसलिए blood भी इस chart में connective tissue है।
beats.on_screen: Two paired branches: supportive → cartilage/bone; fluid → blood/lymph.

beats.say: चौथी main branch Nervous / Neural Tissue है। यहाँ nervous और neural उसी group के नाम हैं; इस chart में इसके नीचे कोई subtype नहीं बनाया गया।
beats.on_screen: Highlight nervous/neural branch with no children.

beats.say: नीचे बीच की body से आसपास के panels की leader lines follow करो। ये किसी body region को बड़े drawing से जोड़ती हैं; सारे drawings एक ही scale पर नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Central body with leader lines highlighted toward four enlarged panels.

beats.say: ऊपर बाएँ Muscular tissue panel में Muscle cells label तीन forms को दिखाता है। Cardiac muscle लाल branching drawing है, जिसकी line heart region से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Muscular panel; highlight collective label, then branching cardiac drawing and heart.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle में लंबे cylindrical fibres का bundle है। Smooth muscle के cells लंबे हैं, लेकिन दोनों सिरों पर पतले होते जाते हैं; shape का यह फर्क देखो।
beats.on_screen: Compare cylindrical skeletal fibres with tapered smooth cells.

beats.say: ऊपर के chart में Striated category यहाँ Skeletal से, और Non-striated यहाँ Smooth से मिलती है। लेकिन cardiac में भी striations होती हैं; अलग branch देखकर उसे non-striated मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Cross-links: Striated ↔ Skeletal; Non-striated ↔ Smooth. Cardiac also striated.

beats.say: Body में Brain सिर के अंदर दिखाया है। उससे नीचे उतरती structure Spinal cord है; shoulder और upper-arm के पास branching structure की ओर Nerve label जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Trace brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerve labels in order.

beats.say: ऊपर दाएँ Nerve tissue panel में purple branched cells हैं। एक cell की ओर Nerve cell label है; यह panel ऊपर की Nervous / Neural Tissue branch से मेल खाता है।

replace_beats.say: शरीर के सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते? Tissue से पूरे शरीर तक का organisation समझकर जवाब ढूँढ़ेंगे।
replace_beats.on_screen: Question beside a body outline.

replace_beats.say: Muscle cells साथ contraction में हिस्सा लेते हैं। यहाँ सिर्फ cells का ढेर नहीं, साझा काम करने वाला group है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Several muscle cells contracting together.

replace_beats.say: Book की definition है: Cells combine to perform same function। Cells मिलकर group बनाते हैं और एक ही काम में हिस्सा देते हैं; यही tissue है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Highlight cells, combine and same function in the definition.

replace_beats.say: तस्वीर में अलग-अलग cells पास रख देने से tissue नहीं बनता। उनके group का साझा function भी होना चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Arbitrary collection versus functional group.

replace_beats.say: इसी definition से अब plant tissues और animal tissues पहचानेंगे।
replace_beats.on_screen: Tissue branches toward plant and animal.

replace_beats.say: यहाँ बाँटने का आधार cells का plant या animal होना है, उनका आकार या काम नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Basis: plant cells or animal cells.

replace_beats.say: Plant की leaf का tissue plant cells से बनता है। तुम्हारा muscle tissue animal cells से बनता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Leaf tissue and human muscle tissue beside their branches.

replace_beats.say: Combine का मतलब सारे cells मिलकर 1 cell बनना नहीं है। यहाँ साथ काम करने वाला organised group समझो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Grouped cells retain individual boundaries.

replace_beats.say: Plant cells से plant tissues; animal cells से animal tissues। ऐसे groups बनने का फायदा क्या है?
replace_beats.on_screen: Completed two-branch tree.

replace_beats.say: Individual cells का workload कम होता है और organisation बनता है। हर cell को शरीर का हर काम अकेले नहीं करना पड़ता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Shared work → reduced individual workload → organisation.

replace_beats.say: Team में कोई सामान सँभाले, कोई पहुँचाए: यही division of labour है। Tissue formation भी cells के बीच शरीर का काम बाँटती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Team sharing tasks, followed by cell groups.

replace_beats.say: अलग tissues covering या movement जैसे अलग काम सँभालते हैं। काम बँटने से हर individual cell पर पूरे शरीर का workload नहीं आता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Tissue groups share covering and movement tasks.

replace_beats.say: Book इन बातों को जोड़ती है: division of labour से कम individual workload और organisation। ये अलग याद करने वाले points नहीं हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Highlight the book's linked claims.

replace_beats.say: कम workload का मतलब cell का अपना जीवन रुकना नहीं है। अपनी देखभाल और energy की जरूरत रहती है; बाँटा गया काम शरीर का है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Shared body work does not eliminate cellular maintenance.

replace_beats.say: Chain देखो: functional groups, division of labour, कम individual workload और organisation। अब इसके levels समझो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Functional groups → division of labour → reduced workload → organisation.

replace_beats.say: पूरे शरीर से अंदर देखो: Organisms से पहले Organ system है। उससे छोटा level Organ है, यानी Tissues और Organ system के बीच।
replace_beats.on_screen: Zoom inward: organism → organ system → organ.

replace_beats.say: Arrows छोटे level का बड़े level में organisation दिखाते हैं। अकेला cell इन stages से गुजरकर पूरा organism नहीं बन जाता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Organisation, not a timed transformation.

replace_beats.say: क्रम है: Cell, Tissues, Organ, Organ system, Organisms। Tissue, cell के बाद और organ से पहले है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Labelled left-to-right hierarchy.

replace_beats.say: अगले labels Columnar epithelium और Ciliated columnar epithelium हैं। दोनों उसी Epithelial Tissue branch से जुड़े हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Trace epithelial connector to columnar and ciliated columnar leaves.

replace_beats.say: अब main branch Muscular Tissue देखो। इसके नीचे बाएँ Striated muscle है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Trace Muscular Tissue to its left subtype.

replace_beats.say: Connective Tissue main group है। नीचे इसकी पहली subdivision Connective tissue proper है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Highlight Connective Tissue and connective tissue proper.

replace_beats.say: Supportive connective tissue में Cartilage और Bone हैं। दोनों एक ही immediate branch के नीचे हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Supportive connective tissue → Cartilage / Bone.

replace_beats.say: Ciliated columnar में लंबे cells के ऊपर बाल जैसी projections हैं। Simple columnar में लंबे cells की 1 layer देखो।
replace_beats.on_screen: Compare ciliated columnar and simple columnar drawings.

beat.say: Organ के अंदर Tissues हैं। Tissues से पहले Cell है, जो इस क्रम का शुरुआती level है।
आखिर में Cuboidal epithelium और Glandular epithelium हैं। इस तरह सभी 6 labels Epithelial Tissue के नीचे आते हैं।
beat.on_screen: Highlight final two epithelial leaves, then all six together.

beat.say: बीच में Non-striated muscle और दाएँ Cardiac muscle है। ये Striated muscle के साथ Muscular Tissue की 3 branches हैं।
beat.on_screen: Highlight middle and right muscle branches, then all three.

beat.say: बाकी subdivisions Supportive connective tissue और Fluid connective tissue हैं। Connective tissue proper के साथ ये 3 groups बनाते हैं।
beat.on_screen: Highlight supportive and fluid subdivisions, then all three intermediate groups.

beat.say: Fluid connective tissue में Blood और Lymph हैं। इसलिए blood भी इस chart में connective tissue है।

beats.say: क्रम है: Cell, Tissues, Organ, Organ system, Organisms। Tissue, cell के बाद और organ से पहले है।
beats.on_screen: Labelled left-to-right hierarchy.

beats.say: अब page 2 का chart animal tissues की categories दिखाता है। नीचे body के आसपास बड़े drawings हैं, ताकि category के साथ उसका रूप और शरीर से connection भी दिखे।
beats.on_screen: Full upper classification tree and lower body overview.

beats.say: ऊपर Animal Tissues से शुरू करो। इसकी 4 main branches हैं: Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue और Nervous / Neural Tissue; line पकड़कर नीचे subtype तक जाओ, ये बदलाव के stages नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace root to each of four main branches.

beats.say: Epithelial Tissue की लंबी line नीचे 6 labels तक जाती है। पहले Simple squamous epithelium और Stratified squamous epithelium पढ़ो; दोनों इसी main branch के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace long epithelial connector; highlight first two leaves.

beats.say: अगले labels Columnar epithelium और Ciliated columnar epithelium हैं। दोनों उसी Epithelial Tissue branch से जुड़े हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace epithelial connector to columnar and ciliated columnar leaves.

beats.say: आखिर में Cuboidal epithelium और Glandular epithelium हैं। इस तरह सभी 6 labels Epithelial Tissue के नीचे आते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight final two epithelial leaves, then all six together.

beats.say: अब main branch Muscular Tissue देखो। इसके नीचे बाएँ Striated muscle है।
beats.on_screen: Trace Muscular Tissue to its left subtype.

beats.say: बीच में Non-striated muscle और दाएँ Cardiac muscle है। ये Striated muscle के साथ Muscular Tissue की 3 branches हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight middle and right muscle branches, then all three.

beats.say: Connective Tissue main group है। नीचे इसकी पहली subdivision Connective tissue proper है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Connective Tissue and connective tissue proper.

beats.say: बाकी subdivisions Supportive connective tissue और Fluid connective tissue हैं। Connective tissue proper के साथ ये 3 groups बनाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight supportive and fluid subdivisions, then all three intermediate groups.

beats.say: Connective tissue proper से Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue और Fibrous tissue निकलते हैं। तीनों एक ही immediate parent के नीचे हैं; इन्हें अलग main tissue groups मत मान लेना।
beats.on_screen: Trace connective tissue proper to its three leaves.

beats.say: Supportive connective tissue में Cartilage और Bone हैं। दोनों एक ही immediate branch के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Supportive connective tissue → Cartilage / Bone.

beats.say: Fluid connective tissue में Blood और Lymph हैं। इसलिए blood भी इस chart में connective tissue है।
beats.on_screen: Fluid connective tissue → Blood / Lymph.

beats.say: चौथी main branch Nervous / Neural Tissue है। यहाँ nervous और neural उसी group के नाम हैं; इस chart में इसके नीचे कोई subtype नहीं बनाया गया।
beats.on_screen: Highlight nervous/neural branch with no children.

beats.say: नीचे बीच की body से आसपास के panels की leader lines follow करो। ये किसी body region को बड़े drawing से जोड़ती हैं; सारे drawings एक ही scale पर नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Central body with leader lines highlighted toward four enlarged panels.

beats.say: ऊपर बाएँ Muscular tissue panel में Muscle cells label तीन forms को दिखाता है। Cardiac muscle लाल branching drawing है, जिसकी line heart region से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Muscular panel; highlight collective label, then branching cardiac drawing and heart.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle में लंबे cylindrical fibres का bundle है। Smooth muscle के cells लंबे हैं, लेकिन दोनों सिरों पर पतले होते जाते हैं; shape का यह फर्क देखो।
beats.on_screen: Compare cylindrical skeletal fibres with tapered smooth cells.

beats.say: ऊपर के chart में Striated category यहाँ Skeletal से, और Non-striated यहाँ Smooth से मिलती है। लेकिन cardiac में भी striations होती हैं; अलग branch देखकर उसे non-striated मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Cross-links: Striated ↔ Skeletal; Non-striated ↔ Smooth. Cardiac also striated.

beats.say: Body में Brain सिर के अंदर दिखाया है। उससे नीचे उतरती structure Spinal cord है; shoulder और upper-arm के पास branching structure की ओर Nerve label जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Trace brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerve labels in order.

beats.say: ऊपर दाएँ Nerve tissue panel में purple branched cells हैं। एक cell की ओर Nerve cell label है; यह panel ऊपर की Nervous / Neural Tissue branch से मेल खाता है।
beats.on_screen: Nerve tissue panel; highlight one branched nerve cell.

beats.say: नीचे बाएँ Epithelial tissue panel में lining और skin दोनों दिखते हैं। Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs वाला label body के digestive tract region से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Epithelial panel and leader line toward gastrointestinal region.

beats.say: Ciliated columnar में लंबे cells के ऊपर बाल जैसी projections हैं। Simple columnar में लंबे cells की 1 layer देखो।
beats.on_screen: Compare ciliated columnar and simple columnar drawings.

beats.say: Simple cuboidal में भी 1 layer है। लेकिन cells लंबे नहीं, छोटे और cube जैसे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the single layer of cube-shaped cells.

beats.say: Simple squamous बहुत पतली, flat sheet जैसा है, tall columnar से साफ अलग। तो इन 4 drawings में cell की ऊँचाई, shape और ऊपर की projections देखकर फर्क पहचान सकते हो।
beats.on_screen: Four labelled epithelial forms together; emphasise thin squamous sheet.

beats.say: Skin surface वाले block में कई layers हैं, और line उसे body के बाहर से जोड़ती है। उसके नीचे पतली boundary Basement membrane है; यह exposed ऊपर वाले हिस्से की उलटी, basal side पर है।
beats.on_screen: Layered skin block; highlight outer side and basement membrane beneath.

beats.say: नीचे दाएँ Connective tissue panel में Tendon, Bone और Fat cells हैं। Tendon पीले parallel fibres का bundle है, जिसकी line wrist और hand region से जुड़ती है।
beats.on_screen: Connective panel, then tendon fibre bundle and wrist association.

beats.say: हल्के रंग की लंबी structure Bone है, जो limb region से जुड़ी है; ऊपर यह supportive connective tissue में थी। Thigh के पास Fat and other Soft padding tissue label है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight bone and thigh padding labels with body links.

beats.say: Fat cells label गोल orange-yellow cells के cluster को दिखाता है। ऊपर के Adipose tissue को नीचे के इन fat cells और fat padding वाले drawing से जोड़कर पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Fat-cell cluster linked back to Adipose tissue leaf.

beats.say: इस figure की जरूरी सीख है: label का parent उसकी connecting line से पहचानो। खासकर Blood और Lymph fluid में, Cartilage और Bone supportive में, और सारे epithelial labels अपनी लंबी line के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the easily misread parent-child relationships.

beats.say: नीचे muscle forms, nerve cells, epithelial forms और tendon-bone-fat के examples उसी ऊपर वाले classification को रूप देते हैं। किसी organ से line जुड़ी होने का मतलब उसमें सिर्फ वही 1 tissue होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Connect four panels back to four main chart branches; note organs contain multiple tissues.

beats.say: अब इन 4 main types को उनके मुख्य काम से अलग पहचानो। Page 3 उसी visual overview को function के साथ जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Four tissue names beside an empty function column.

beats.say: हमारे शरीर के main tissue groups Epithelial, Muscular, Neural और Connective हैं। ये बराबर level की 4 categories हैं, किसी एक के नीचे बाकी 3 नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Body tissues → four equal-level branches.

beats.say: Epithelial covering या lining देता है, जैसे अभी skin और hollow organs में देखा। Muscular movement में मदद करता है; Neural stimuli पर response देता है; Connective support करता है, जोड़ता है और cushioning देता है।
beats.on_screen: Fill each function beside its tissue with matching figure example.

beats.say: Stimulus मतलब ऐसा बदलाव जिसे detect किया जा सके, जैसे touch या temperature। और covering को support से मत मिलाना: covering के लिए Epithelial, support-link-cushion के लिए Connective पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Stimulus: detectable change. Contrast covering with support and cushioning.

beats.say: आखिरी बार काम से नाम जोड़ो: covering-lining, Epithelial; movement, Muscular; stimuli का response, Neural; support-link-cushion, Connective। अगले video में Epithelial tissue की layers, shapes और काम को खोलकर समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Completed four-branch function tree; highlight Epithelial for next lesson.

frame.process: Tissue organisation distributes the organism's work.

beats.say: शरीर के सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते? Tissue से पूरे शरीर तक का organisation समझकर जवाब ढूँढ़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Question beside a body outline.

beats.say: Muscle cells साथ contraction में हिस्सा लेते हैं। यहाँ सिर्फ cells का ढेर नहीं, साझा काम करने वाला group है।
beats.on_screen: Several muscle cells contracting together.

beats.say: Book की definition है: Cells combine to perform same function। Cells मिलकर group बनाते हैं और एक ही काम में हिस्सा देते हैं; यही tissue है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight cells, combine and same function in the definition.

beats.say: तस्वीर में अलग-अलग cells पास रख देने से tissue नहीं बनता। उनके group का साझा function भी होना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Arbitrary collection versus functional group.

beats.say: इसी definition से अब plant tissues और animal tissues पहचानेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Tissue branches toward plant and animal.

beats.say: यहाँ बाँटने का आधार cells का plant या animal होना है, उनका आकार या काम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Basis: plant cells or animal cells.

beats.say: ऊपर tissue रखो और नीचे 2 रास्ते बनाओ। Plant cells मिलें तो plant tissues; animal cells मिलें तो animal tissues।
beats.on_screen: Tissue → Plant tissues / Animal tissues.

beats.say: Plant की leaf का tissue plant cells से बनता है। तुम्हारा muscle tissue animal cells से बनता है।
beats.on_screen: Leaf tissue and human muscle tissue beside their branches.

beats.say: Combine का मतलब सारे cells मिलकर 1 cell बनना नहीं है। यहाँ साथ काम करने वाला organised group समझो।
beats.on_screen: Grouped cells retain individual boundaries.

beats.say: Plant cells से plant tissues; animal cells से animal tissues। ऐसे groups बनने का फायदा क्या है?
beats.on_screen: Completed two-branch tree.

beats.say: Individual cells का workload कम होता है और organisation बनता है। हर cell को शरीर का हर काम अकेले नहीं करना पड़ता।
beats.on_screen: Shared work → reduced individual workload → organisation.

beats.say: Team में कोई सामान सँभाले, कोई पहुँचाए: यही division of labour है। Tissue formation भी cells के बीच शरीर का काम बाँटती है।
beats.on_screen: Team sharing tasks, followed by cell groups.

beats.say: अलग tissues covering या movement जैसे अलग काम सँभालते हैं। काम बँटने से हर individual cell पर पूरे शरीर का workload नहीं आता।
beats.on_screen: Tissue groups share covering and movement tasks.

beats.say: Book इन बातों को जोड़ती है: division of labour से कम individual workload और organisation। ये अलग याद करने वाले points नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the book's linked claims.

beats.say: कम workload का मतलब cell का अपना जीवन रुकना नहीं है। अपनी देखभाल और energy की जरूरत रहती है; बाँटा गया काम शरीर का है।
beats.on_screen: Shared body work does not eliminate cellular maintenance.

beats.say: Chain देखो: functional groups, division of labour, कम individual workload और organisation। अब इसके levels समझो।
beats.on_screen: Functional groups → division of labour → reduced workload → organisation.

beats.say: पूरा living being organism है। Book का क्रम Cell से शुरू होकर Tissues, Organ, Organ system और आखिर में Organisms तक जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Full hierarchy beside a complete organism.

beats.say: पूरे शरीर से अंदर देखो: Organisms से पहले Organ system है। उससे छोटा level Organ है, यानी Tissues और Organ system के बीच।
beats.on_screen: Zoom inward: organism → organ system → organ.

beats.say: Organ के अंदर Tissues हैं। Tissues से पहले Cell है, जो इस क्रम का शुरुआती level है।
beats.on_screen: Continue inward: organ → tissues → cell.

beats.say: Cells साझा काम के लिए tissue बनाते हैं। कई tissues organ में साथ काम करते हैं; organs मिलकर system का बड़ा काम सँभालते हैं, और systems मिलकर organism को चलाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Connect each nested level to its contribution.

beats.say: Arrows छोटे level का बड़े level में organisation दिखाते हैं। इसका मतलब यह नहीं कि अकेला cell इन stages में बदलता हुआ पूरा organism बन जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Organisation, not a timed transformation.

beats.say: क्रम है: Cell, Tissues, Organ, Organ system, Organisms। Tissue, cell के बाद और organ से पहले है।
beats.on_screen: Labelled left-to-right hierarchy.

beats.say: अब page 2 का chart animal tissues की categories दिखाता है। नीचे body के आसपास बड़े drawings हैं, ताकि category के साथ उसका रूप और शरीर से connection भी दिखे।
beats.on_screen: Full upper classification tree and lower body overview.

beats.say: ऊपर Animal Tissues से शुरू करो। इसकी 4 main branches हैं: Epithelial Tissue, Muscular Tissue, Connective Tissue और Nervous / Neural Tissue; line पकड़कर नीचे subtype तक जाओ, ये बदलाव के stages नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace root to each of four main branches.

beats.say: Epithelial Tissue की लंबी line नीचे 6 labels तक जाती है। पहले Simple squamous epithelium और Stratified squamous epithelium पढ़ो; दोनों इसी main branch के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace long epithelial connector; highlight first two leaves.

beats.say: अगले labels Columnar epithelium और Ciliated columnar epithelium हैं। दोनों उसी Epithelial Tissue branch से जुड़े हैं।
beats.on_screen: Trace epithelial connector to columnar and ciliated columnar leaves.

beats.say: आखिर में Cuboidal epithelium और Glandular epithelium हैं। इस तरह सभी 6 labels Epithelial Tissue के नीचे आते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight final two epithelial leaves, then all six together.

beats.say: अब main branch Muscular Tissue देखो। इसके नीचे बाएँ Striated muscle है।
beats.on_screen: Trace Muscular Tissue to its left subtype.

beats.say: बीच में Non-striated muscle और दाएँ Cardiac muscle है। ये Striated muscle के साथ Muscular Tissue की 3 branches हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight middle and right muscle branches, then all three.

beats.say: Connective Tissue main group है। नीचे इसकी पहली subdivision Connective tissue proper है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Connective Tissue and connective tissue proper.

beats.say: बाकी subdivisions Supportive connective tissue और Fluid connective tissue हैं। Connective tissue proper के साथ ये 3 groups बनाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight supportive and fluid subdivisions, then all three intermediate groups.

beats.say: Connective tissue proper से Areolar tissue, Adipose tissue और Fibrous tissue निकलते हैं। तीनों एक ही immediate parent के नीचे हैं; इन्हें अलग main tissue groups मत मान लेना।
beats.on_screen: Trace connective tissue proper to its three leaves.

beats.say: Supportive connective tissue में Cartilage और Bone हैं। दोनों एक ही immediate branch के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Supportive connective tissue → Cartilage / Bone.

beats.say: Fluid connective tissue में Blood और Lymph हैं। इसलिए blood भी इस chart में connective tissue है।
beats.on_screen: Fluid connective tissue → Blood / Lymph.

beats.say: चौथी main branch Nervous / Neural Tissue है। यहाँ nervous और neural उसी group के नाम हैं; इस chart में इसके नीचे कोई subtype नहीं बनाया गया।
beats.on_screen: Highlight nervous/neural branch with no children.

beats.say: नीचे बीच की body से आसपास के panels की leader lines follow करो। ये किसी body region को बड़े drawing से जोड़ती हैं; सारे drawings एक ही scale पर नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Central body with leader lines highlighted toward four enlarged panels.

beats.say: ऊपर बाएँ Muscular tissue panel में Muscle cells label तीन forms को दिखाता है। Cardiac muscle लाल branching drawing है, जिसकी line heart region से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Muscular panel; highlight collective label, then branching cardiac drawing and heart.

beats.say: Skeletal muscle में लंबे cylindrical fibres का bundle है। Smooth muscle के cells लंबे हैं, लेकिन दोनों सिरों पर पतले होते जाते हैं; shape का यह फर्क देखो।
beats.on_screen: Compare cylindrical skeletal fibres with tapered smooth cells.

beats.say: ऊपर के chart में Striated category यहाँ Skeletal से, और Non-striated यहाँ Smooth से मिलती है। लेकिन cardiac में भी striations होती हैं; अलग branch देखकर उसे non-striated मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Cross-links: Striated ↔ Skeletal; Non-striated ↔ Smooth. Cardiac also striated.

beats.say: Body में Brain सिर के अंदर दिखाया है। उससे नीचे उतरती structure Spinal cord है; shoulder और upper-arm के पास branching structure की ओर Nerve label जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Trace brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerve labels in order.

beats.say: ऊपर दाएँ Nerve tissue panel में purple branched cells हैं। एक cell की ओर Nerve cell label है; यह panel ऊपर की Nervous / Neural Tissue branch से मेल खाता है।
beats.on_screen: Nerve tissue panel; highlight one branched nerve cell.

beats.say: नीचे बाएँ Epithelial tissue panel में lining और skin दोनों दिखते हैं। Lining of gastrointestinal tract and other hollow organs वाला label body के digestive tract region से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Epithelial panel and leader line toward gastrointestinal region.

beats.say: Ciliated columnar में लंबे cells के ऊपर बाल जैसी projections हैं। Simple columnar में लंबे cells की 1 layer देखो।
beats.on_screen: Compare ciliated columnar and simple columnar drawings.

beats.say: Simple cuboidal में भी 1 layer है। लेकिन cells लंबे नहीं, छोटे और cube जैसे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the single layer of cube-shaped cells.

beats.say: Simple squamous बहुत पतली, flat sheet जैसा है, tall columnar से साफ अलग। तो इन 4 drawings में cell की ऊँचाई, shape और ऊपर की projections देखकर फर्क पहचान सकते हो।
beats.on_screen: Four labelled epithelial forms together; emphasise thin squamous sheet.

beats.say: Skin surface वाले block में कई layers हैं, और line उसे body के बाहर से जोड़ती है। उसके नीचे पतली boundary Basement membrane है; यह exposed ऊपर वाले हिस्से की उलटी, basal side पर है।
beats.on_screen: Layered skin block; highlight outer side and basement membrane beneath.

beats.say: नीचे दाएँ Connective tissue panel में Tendon, Bone और Fat cells हैं। Tendon पीले parallel fibres का bundle है, जिसकी line wrist और hand region से जुड़ती है।
beats.on_screen: Connective panel, then tendon fibre bundle and wrist association.

beats.say: हल्के रंग की लंबी structure Bone है, जो limb region से जुड़ी है; ऊपर यह supportive connective tissue में थी। Thigh के पास Fat and other Soft padding tissue label है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight bone and thigh padding labels with body links.

beats.say: Fat cells label गोल orange-yellow cells के cluster को दिखाता है। ऊपर के Adipose tissue को नीचे के इन fat cells और fat padding वाले drawing से जोड़कर पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Fat-cell cluster linked back to Adipose tissue leaf.

beats.say: इस figure की जरूरी सीख है: label का parent उसकी connecting line से पहचानो। खासकर Blood और Lymph fluid में, Cartilage और Bone supportive में, और सारे epithelial labels अपनी लंबी line के नीचे हैं।
beats.on_screen: Highlight the easily misread parent-child relationships.

beats.say: नीचे muscle forms, nerve cells, epithelial forms और tendon-bone-fat के examples उसी ऊपर वाले classification को रूप देते हैं। किसी organ से line जुड़ी होने का मतलब उसमें सिर्फ वही 1 tissue होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Connect four panels back to four main chart branches; note organs contain multiple tissues.

beats.say: अब इन 4 main types को उनके मुख्य काम से अलग पहचानो। Page 3 उसी visual overview को function के साथ जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Four tissue names beside an empty function column.

beats.say: हमारे शरीर के main tissue groups Epithelial, Muscular, Neural और Connective हैं। ये बराबर level की 4 categories हैं, किसी एक के नीचे बाकी 3 नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Body tissues → four equal-level branches.

beats.say: Epithelial covering या lining देता है, जैसे अभी skin और hollow organs में देखा। Muscular movement में मदद करता है; Neural stimuli पर response देता है; Connective support करता है, जोड़ता है और cushioning देता है।
beats.on_screen: Fill each function beside its tissue with matching figure example.

beats.say: Stimulus मतलब ऐसा बदलाव जिसे detect किया जा सके, जैसे touch या temperature। और covering को support से मत मिलाना: covering के लिए Epithelial, support-link-cushion के लिए Connective पहचानो।
beats.on_screen: Stimulus: detectable change. Contrast covering with support and cushioning.

beats.say: आखिरी बार काम से नाम जोड़ो: covering-lining, Epithelial; movement, Muscular; stimuli का response, Neural; support-link-cushion, Connective। अगले video में Epithelial tissue की layers, shapes और काम को खोलकर समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Completed four-branch function tree; highlight Epithelial for next lesson.

Cell से पूरे शरीर तक') covering pages 1 to 3: tissue definition, plant/animal tissue division, division of labour, levels of biological organisation, the complete animal-tissue classification tree and body overview figure, and the four main animal tissue functions.

decisions.reason: The maker consciously reserved detailed histological mechanisms (such as keratinisation or microvilli vs cilia) for the upcoming dedicated topic videos so the 49-item figure walkthrough fits comfortably in the 9-minute window; this is pedagogically sound and well-documented in the maker's notes.

problems.fix: No change required for this overview video since detailed epithelial, connective, muscular and neural mechanisms are taught in subsequent videos (v2 onwards), or optionally add one brief phrase in b38/b40 if extra time permits.

The script uses natural, conversational Hinglish suitable for UPSC/State PCS aspirants, with clear teacher cues and smooth transitions.
Nothing from the book pages is cut short or left as 'etc.'; all 49 items of the page-2 figure and all text/diagram items on pages 1 and 3 are explicitly named and explained.

The video is planned for 9 minutes across 3 pages (including a dense 49-item composite figure page), and the spoken word count (~1,020 words across 56 beats) falls cleanly within the 1,001-1,339 word target window.

The script flows logically from the hook and definition to plant/animal classification, division of labour, biological hierarchy, the page-2 visual overview, and the page-3 functional classification without side-tracks.
Prerequisite concepts (contraction, covering, lining) are woven in naturally without exceeding the 2-beat reminder limit.
Hindi words are in Devanagari, technical English terms are in Roman script, sentences are short and spoken-friendly, and difficult Hindi words avoided.
All 61 must_cover item IDs are claimed in covers_item_ids and genuinely taught in the corresponding beats, and all claimed question IDs in answers[] are truly answered.
